score.meaning: Strong, coherent authored acting with preserved tiny anatomy and readable thought changes in source/selected frames. Remaining small-scale invitation and afterthought ambiguity keeps this below excellent. This number covers the explicitly inspected staging, not subjective continuous playback or human comprehension.

strengths: Investigate & share has a specific intention: antenna attention precedes gaze, gaze precedes head/wing orientation, glasses and a short consideration hold precede return to the visitor. It is more characterful than a face-label swap. The visible screen-right question gives the attention a cause.

The investigation and wry variants share the same pre-afterthought action; the extra beat is an optional interpretation rather than a different anatomy or an unrelated second routine. Owner preference grounds Investigate & share as personal-fit lead without claiming audience validation.
One peek preserves a compact pretend-sleep setup and a held reveal. The open half-eye, antenna change and cheek mitten support the same joke; no limb enlargement or looping wing display is needed.

Surprise clearly separates an early O-mouth/eye registration from later head and wing response. The authored 140ms facial onset and 180ms replay entry preserve urgency without moving every part at once.

Hop frames and source now separate foot contact at1060ms from head follow-through toward1140ms, then recovery by1410ms. Body descent crosses the900ms wing reversal instead of stopping there; the unchanged body and stub feet support a small-weight action.

Thinking, focused, grateful, shy and worried use different mitten relationships. The worried supporting hand sits below the other hand, avoiding the earlier stronger hand-clasp resemblance; the chin action remains one-handed.

Compatible difficult-emotion entries retain emotional posture and facial intention, while the independent interruption tests report bounded poses and completion. The inspected night sheets preserve the same acting geometry.

workflowChanges.change: Before implementation, cast each acting channel as lead/support/static and write a causal timeline: antenna notices, gaze follows, head turns, wing supports, hand offers. Record why a beat overlaps or waits; tie secondary follow-through to contact or thought change, not arbitrary equal delays.

Review purpose, repetition frequency, interruption and reduced motion separately from aesthetic enthusiasm. Produce named evidence-backed defects; do not approve because tests pass or a target score was requested.

Use precise terms—anticipation, follow-through, orchestration, interruption, held pose—when handing off changes. Distinguish an acting hold from UI latency and a deterministic export frame rate from observed browser jank.

Inventory the rAF driver and SVG updates, then profile a real target device with concurrent page work before proposing optimizations. Name the measured cause and preserve visual correctness; do not add will-change or replace geometry on intuition.

Maintain frame timestamps and source hashes, inspect decoded frame evidence directly, and explicitly distinguish sampled motion analysis from continuous playback. Reuse existing exports and focused samples for disputed beats.

Keep character choreography and product-control motion as separate reviews. Website controls should follow frequency and responsiveness budgets; the character can retain intentional anticipation and thought holds when it remains optional, interruptible and reduced-motion safe.
